# Metadata fixtures

The fixtures contain 150 ms of generated silence, Unicode tags, explicit artist
lists, track/disc totals, and deterministic PNG covers larger than one Ogg page.
The back cover is deliberately stored before the front cover. MP4 does not carry
picture roles, so its expected result is the first picture.

`tags.ape` uses TagLib 2.3.2's `tests/data/mac-399.ape` sample with the same generated
tags and pictures applied. Its upstream source and licenses are retained under
`modules/astra-library-scanner/third_party/taglib` (MPL 1.1 / LGPL 2.1).
All other audio and both PNGs are generated by
`scripts/generate-metadata-fixtures.py`; it takes the fixture writer executable
built from `scripts/metadata-fixture-writer.cpp` and the vendored TagLib library.
The writer is used only to prepare test assets and is never shipped in the app.
Additional Opus fixtures cover alternate aliases and repeated ARTIST fields,
an invalid front cover with a valid back cover, and missing tags.

`desktop.json` records `music-metadata` results from desktop commit `7e9d3dd`,
using `duration: true` to read complete Opus/Ogg tags. Android compares the core
fields with this reference. Regenerate it with
`node scripts/capture-metadata-reference.mjs ../astra`.
Two deliberate artwork/ordering differences:

- That desktop version's `selectCover` selects the first image even when it is a
  back cover. Android asserts the actual generated front-cover bytes whenever
  the container records picture roles.
- The desktop ASF mapper reverses custom ARTISTS values and misreads these ASF
  picture bytes. Android verifies complete artist membership, keeps TagLib's
  source order, and validates the generated front PNG directly.

ID3v2.3 is remuxed with ffmpeg. Its metadata reflects v2.3's scalar custom-text
limitations; the other MP3 fixture uses ID3v2.4 with repeated custom fields.
